'''Sathamangalam Ranga Iyengar Srinivasa Varadhan''', {{post nominals|list= [[Fellow of the Royal Society|FRS]]}} (born 2 January 1940) is an [[Indian American]] [[mathematician]] and [[statistician]]. He is known for his fundamental contributions to [[probability theory]] and in particular for creating a unified theory of [[Large deviations theory|large deviations]].<ref name=Ramachandran>{{cite web|last=Ramachandran|first=R.|title=Science of chance|url=http://frontlineonnet.com/fl2407/stories/20070420001909700.htm|work=Frontline|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071211145135/http://www.frontlineonnet.com/fl2407/stories/20070420001909700.htm|archive-date=11 December 2007|location=India|date=7–20 April 2007}}</ref> He is regarded as one of the fundamental contributors to the theory of [[diffusion process]]es with an orientation towards the refinement and further development of Itô’s [[stochastic calculus]].<ref>{{cite book |last1=Varadhan |first1=S. R. Srinivasa |title=Essentials of integration theory for analysis |url=https://search.library.wisc.edu/catalog/9913182061202121 |publisher=Springer, [2020] ©2020 |date=2020}}</ref> In the year 2007, he won the [[Abel Prize]].<ref>{{cite web |title=2007: Srinivasa S. R. Varadhan {{!}} The Abel Prize |url=https://abelprize.no/abel-prize-laureates/2007 |website=abelprize.no}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Indian wins Norway's Abel Prize for Mathematics |url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/india/indian-wins-norway-s-abel-prize-for-mathematics/story-UXUQjRsvihBEnB80xgBXKL.html#:~:text=Indian%2Dborn%20New%20York%20University,fundamental%20contributions%20to%20probability%20theory. |work=Hindustan Times |date=23 March 2007 |language=en}}</ref>

==Early life and education ==
Srinivasa was born into a [[Hindu]] [[Tamil Brahmin]] [[Iyengar]] family in 1940 <ref>{{Cite web|title= Srinivasa Varadhan |url=http://www.abelprisen.no/binfil/download.php?tid=56998|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161105070617/http://www.abelprisen.no/binfil/download.php?tid=56998|archive-date = 5 November 2016}}</ref> in Chennai (then [[Madras]]). In 1953, his family migrated to [[Kolkata]]. He grew up in [[Chennai]] and [[Kolkata]].<ref>interview-with-srinivasa-varadhan/ Interview with Srinivasa Varadhan], http://gonitsora.com</ref> 

Varadhan received his undergraduate degree in 1959 and his postgraduate degree in 1960 from [[Presidency College, Chennai]].  He received his doctorate from [[Indian Statistical Institute]] in 1963 under [[C R Rao]],<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=33923}}</ref><ref>[http://www.isical.ac.in/~deanweb/ALU_DEGR.HTM List of degree / diploma / certificate recipients of ISI], web site at the [[Indian Statistical Institute]]. Retrieved 22 March 2007.</ref> who arranged for [[Andrey Kolmogorov]] to be present at Varadhan's thesis defence.<ref>[http://www.allvoices.com/people/S._R._Srinivasa_Varadhan S. R. Srinivasa Varadhan's Biography], Allvoices. Retrieved 1 August 2010.</ref> He was one of the "famous four" (the others being [[Ramaswamy Ranga Rao]], [[K. R. Parthasarathy (probabilist)|K R Parthasarathy]], and [[Veeravalli S. Varadarajan|Veeravalli S Varadarajan]]) in [[Indian Statistical Institute|ISI]] during 1956–1963.<ref>{{cite web|first1=Kalyan Bidhan |last1=Sinha |first2=B. V. |last2=Rajarama Bhat|title=S. R. Srinivasa Varadhan|url=https://www.math.lsu.edu/cosa/6-1-00%5Bpartha%5D.pdf|publisher=[[Louisiana State University]]}}</ref>

==Career==
Since 1963, he has worked at the [[Courant Institute of Mathematical Sciences]] at [[New York University]], where he was at first a postdoctoral fellow (1963–66), strongly recommended by [[Monroe D. Donsker|Monroe D Donsker]]. Here he met [[Daniel Stroock]], who became a close colleague and co-author. In an article in the ''Notices of the American Mathematical Society'', Stroock recalls these early years:
{{Blockquote|Varadhan, whom everyone calls Raghu, came to these shores from his native India in the fall of 1963. He arrived by plane at Idlewild Airport and proceeded to Manhattan by bus. His destination was that famous institution with the modest name, The Courant Institute of Mathematical Sciences, where he had been given a postdoctoral fellowship. Varadhan was assigned to one of the many windowless offices in the Courant building, which used to be a hat factory. Yet despite the somewhat humble surroundings, from these offices flowed a remarkably large fraction of the post-war mathematics of which America is justly proud.}}
Varadhan is currently a professor at the Courant Institute.<ref name="steele">[http://www.ams.org/notices/199611/comm-steele.pdf Announcement of the] 1996 [[Steele Prize]]s at the [[American Mathematical Society]] web site. Retrieved 21 February 2007.</ref><ref name="abelbio">Srinivasa Varadhan is known as S R S Varadhan for short and Raghu to his friends and colleagues. His father, Ranga Iyengar, was a science teacher who became the Principal of the Board High School in Ponneri
[http://www.abelprisen.no/nedlastning/2007/biography_en.pdf Biography] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070421124112/http://www.abelprisen.no/nedlastning/2007/biography_en.pdf |date=21 April 2007 }} (PDF), from the [[Abel Prize]] web site. Retrieved 22 March 2007.</ref> He is known for his work with [[Daniel W Stroock]] on [[diffusion process]]es, and for his work on [[large deviations]] with [[Monroe D. Donsker|Monroe D Donsker]]. He has chaired the Mathematical Sciences jury for the [[Infosys Prize]] from 2009 and was the chief guest in 2020.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Infosys Prize - Jury 2020|url=http://www.infosys-science-foundation.com/prize/jury/jury-2020.asp|access-date=2020-12-10|website=www.infosys-science-foundation.com}}</ref>

His son, [[Ashok Varadhan]], is an executive at financial firm [[Goldman Sachs]].<ref>{{cite web |title = Can Goldman's Trading 'Rainmaker' Bring Back the Glory Days? |first = Sridhar |last = Natarajan |date = July 1, 2019 |work = Bloomberg |url = https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2019-07-01/can-goldman-s-trading-rainmaker-bring-back-the-glory-days}}</ref>

==Awards and honours==
Varadhan's awards and honours include the [[National Medal of Science]] (2010) from President [[Barack Obama]], "the highest honour bestowed by the [[United States government]] on scientists, engineers and inventors".<ref>{{cite web|url=https://obamawhitehouse.archives.gov/the-press-office/2011/09/27/president-obama-honors-nation-s-top-scientists-and-innovators |title=President Obama Honors Nation's Top Scientists and Innovators |date=27 September 2011 |via=[[NARA|National Archives]] |work=[[whitehouse.gov]] |access-date=28 September 2011}}</ref> He also received the [[Birkhoff Prize]] (1994), the Margaret and Herman Sokol Award of the Faculty of Arts and Sciences, New York University (1995), and the [[Leroy P. Steele Prize for Seminal Contribution to Research|Leroy P Steele Prize for Seminal Contribution to Research]] (1996) from the [[American Mathematical Society]], awarded for his work with [[Daniel W. Stroock|Daniel W Stroock]] on [[diffusion process]]es.<ref name="ams_notices_1996">{{cite journal|url=http://www.ams.org/notices/199611/comm-steele.pdf |title=1996 Steele Prizes |journal=[[Notices of the American Mathematical Society]] |volume=43 |issue=11 |pages=1340–1347 |date=November 1996 |access-date=29 September 2011}}</ref> He was awarded the [[Abel Prize]] in 2007 for his work on [[large deviations]] with [[Monroe D. Donsker|Monroe D Donsker]].<ref name="steele" /><ref>{{Cite web |title=2007: Srinivasa S. R. Varadhan |url=https://abelprize.no/abel-prize-laureates/2007 |access-date=August 22, 2022 |website=www.abelprize.no}}</ref> In 2008, the Government of India awarded him the [[Padma Bhushan]].<ref name="Padma Awards">{{cite web | url=http://mha.nic.in/sites/upload_files/mha/files/LST-PDAWD-2013.pdf | title=Padma Awards | publisher=Ministry of Home Affairs, Government of India | year=2015 | access-date=21 July 2015 | archive-date=15 October 2015 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151015193758/http://mha.nic.in/sites/upload_files/mha/files/LST-PDAWD-2013.pdf | url-status=dead }}</ref> and in 2023, he was awarded India's second highest civilian honor [[Padma Vibhushan]].<ref>[https://www.padmaawards.gov.in/Content/PadmaAwardees2023.pdf Padma Awardees]</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=January 25, 2023|title=Padma honours: Full list of awardees|url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/india/padma-vibhushan-padma-bhushan-padma-shree-padma-awards-full-list/articleshow/97325138.cms |access-date=2023-01-25 |website=The Times of India |language=en}}</ref> He also has two honorary degrees from Université Pierre et Marie Curie in Paris (2003) and from [[Indian Statistical Institute]] in Kolkata, India (2004).

Varadhan is a member of the [[United States National Academy of Sciences|US National Academy of Sciences]] (1995),<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nasonline.org/site/Dir?sid=1011&view=basic&pg=srch |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20051025074536/http://www.nasonline.org/site/Dir?sid=1011&view=basic&pg=srch |url-status=dead |archive-date=25 October 2005 |title=NAS Membership Directory |publisher=[[United States National Academy of Sciences|U.S. National Academy of Sciences]] |access-date=10 June 2011}} Search with Last Name is "Varadhan".</ref> and the [[Norwegian Academy of Science and Letters]] (2009).<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.dnva.no/c26849/artikkel/vis.html?tid=40116|title=Gruppe 1: Matematiske fag|publisher=[[Norwegian Academy of Science and Letters]]|language=no|access-date=10 June 2011|archive-date=10 November 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131110152102/http://www.dnva.no/c26849/artikkel/vis.html?tid=40116|url-status=dead}}</ref> He was elected to Fellow of the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]] (1988),<ref name=AAAS>{{cite web|title=Book of Members, 1780–2010: Chapter V|url=http://www.amacad.org/publications/BookofMembers/ChapterV.pdf|publisher=[[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]]|access-date=10 June 2011}}</ref> the [[Third World Academy of Sciences]] (1988), the [[Institute of Mathematical Statistics]] (1991), the [[Royal Society]] (1998),<ref>{{cite web|url=http://royalsociety.org/uploadedFiles/Royal_Society_Content/about-us/fellowship/Fellows_and_Foreign_Members.pdf |title=Fellows of the Royal Society |publisher=[[Royal Society]] |access-date=10 June 2011}}</ref> the [[Indian Academy of Sciences]] (2004), the [[Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics]] (2009),<ref>{{cite web|url=http://fellows.siam.org/index.php?sort=year&value=2009 |title=SIAM Fellows: Class of 2009 |publisher=[[Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics]] |access-date=10 June 2011}}</ref> and the [[American Mathematical Society]] (2012).<ref>[http://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society]. Retrieved 28 August 2013.</ref>
